source_groups.explanation: Skin, hair, dander, feathers and droppings from pets and farm animals.
Antibiotics, pain relievers, numbing medicines and vitamins.
Mites and mixed dusts found in homes, stores and workplaces.
Stinging insects, cockroaches, mosquitoes, flies and moths.
Mould spores and yeast found in damp places and on the body.
Pollen from weeds and trees, plus one farm crop.
Fish, meats, shellfish and egg parts.
Milk products plus coffee, tea, chocolate, tofu, yeast and mushrooms.
Nuts, seeds, grains, pulses and dried fruit.
Common spices, herbs and curry blends.
Latex, fibres, silk, wool and henna that people touch or handle.
Worms that can infect people and may produce IgE.
A single general blood marker that counts all IgE antibodies.

canonical_categories.explanation: Tiny flakes of skin, hair and body proteins from furry animals can float in the air and settle on surfaces.
Feathers, dust and dried droppings from pet and farm birds can carry proteins that some people become sensitized to.
Microscopic mites live in bedding, carpets and soft furnishings and are a common indoor trigger worldwide.
These mites live in stored grains, flour and damp food-storage areas rather than in beds.
These tests use dust collected from homes, hay or old books, which contains a mix of materials.
Dust and fibres from plants such as tobacco, jute and cotton can be inhaled or touched during work or hobbies.
Fibres from sheep wool and silk are used in clothing and textiles and may be handled at work.
Latex is a rubber material found in gloves, balloons and medical products.
Henna is a plant dye used for skin and hair decoration.
Venom is injected during a sting, so this is different from everyday environmental exposure.
Cockroach body parts and droppings can become part of household dust, especially in kitchens and damp areas.
Moths, mosquitoes and houseflies are common around homes and can sometimes trigger allergy symptoms.
Pollen from grasses is carried in the air in certain seasons and is a common cause of hay fever.
Pollen from common weeds is released into the air in certain seasons.
Pollen from trees is carried by wind in certain seasons and can affect the nose, eyes and chest.
Pollen from farm crops such as oilseed rape can be released in large amounts near fields.
Moulds are tiny fungi that grow in damp places and release spores into the air.
Candida is a yeast that normally lives on human skin, in the mouth and in the gut.
These are common antibiotics related to penicillin that doctors use for many infections.
These antibiotics belong to several different families used for a variety of infections.
These common medicines relieve pain, inflammation and fever.
These medicines numb the skin or mouth and are used in creams, sprays and dental or minor procedures.
This group includes vitamins and a cough medicine that people may take as tablets, syrups or injections.
Onion and garlic are strongly flavoured vegetables used in most Indian cooking.
Cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli and radish belong to the same plant family.
Tomato, potato, brinjal and capsicum belong to the nightshade plant family.
Pumpkin and cucumber belong to the gourd plant family.
Spinach and lettuce are eaten for their leaves, raw or cooked.
Carrot, beetroot and sweet potato are vegetables that grow underground.
These foods come from legume plants and include soya products such as tofu.
Apple, peach, plum, cherry, apricot and strawberry belong to the rose plant family.
Citrus fruits such as orange are juicy fruits rich in vitamin C.
Watermelon and melon are juicy fruits from the gourd plant family.
Mango, banana, papaya, pineapple, guava, lychee and kiwi are widely eaten warm-climate fruits.
These are fresh and dried fruits that do not fit into the other fruit groups.
Rice, wheat, barley, oats and maize are grains used for staple foods.
These are finfish commonly eaten fresh, dried or tinned.
Prawns, crab and lobster are shellfish with a hard outer shell.
Mutton, beef and pork are meats from mammals.
Chicken, turkey and duck are meats from farmed birds.
These tests look at the whole egg or at its white and yolk separately.
Milk, curd, yogurt, cheese and milk protein come from cow's milk.
Peanut is a legume that is commonly eaten roasted, in chutneys, sweets and snacks.
Almond, walnut, cashew, hazelnut and pistachio are nuts that grow on trees.
Coconut and coconut milk are widely used in cooking in many parts of India.
Sesame, sunflower, pumpkin, poppy and flax seeds are eaten whole, ground or pressed for oil.
Spices come from seeds, bark, roots or buds of plants and are used to flavour food.
Herbs such as mint, basil, thyme and oregano are leafy plants used to flavour food.
Curry powder is a blend of several spices that varies between brands and recipes.
These plant-based drinks and treats are enjoyed daily by many people.
Mushrooms are edible fungi, and yeast is used in baking and brewing.
Roundworms such as Ascaris and the dog roundworm Toxocara can infect people through soil, dirty hands or contaminated food.
Anisakis is a worm that can live in sea fish and cause illness or allergy when infected fish is eaten.
Total IgE counts all IgE antibodies in your blood. It is a general marker and not a test for one allergen.

C_SENS.patient_text: A positive blood test shows your immune system has made IgE to this substance. This is called sensitization. It does not prove that the substance is causing your symptoms.

C_CLASS.patient_text: The class or value on your report shows how much IgE was found. It does not show how severe a reaction could be, and a higher value does not mean a worse reaction.

C_NEG.patient_text: A negative or low result does not rule out an allergy, and it does not make something safe. Your history and your doctor's advice matter more than this test alone.

C_TOTAL.patient_text: Total IgE is a general marker. It cannot confirm allergy, cannot show which substance you react to, and cannot show how severe any allergy might be.

C_ANIMAL.patient_text: A positive result may involve proteins that several animals share. It does not show that your own pet is the cause, so speak to an allergist before any decision about a pet.

C_BIRD.patient_text: Feathers, droppings and bird products can contain different proteins. A positive result for one bird part does not show which bird or which part matters for you.

C_MITE.patient_text: Dust mite, storage mite and cockroach results often appear together, and they share a protein with shellfish. A positive result does not show which source is responsible.

C_MIXED.patient_text: This test uses a mixture of materials. The result cannot say which part you react to, so it is less specific than a test for a single source.

C_OCC.patient_text: These materials matter most if you touch or breathe them at work or during a hobby. A blood test alone cannot show whether your work is causing symptoms.

C_VENOM.patient_text: A positive venom result shows sensitization and does not prove you will react to the next sting. Anyone with a body wide reaction to a sting should see an allergist.

C_INSECT_XR.patient_text: Cockroach results often appear together with dust mite results, so the true source can be hard to tell apart without your doctor's review.

C_INSECT_OTHER.patient_text: Blood tests for mosquito, housefly and moth have limited published support. A positive result alone does not explain your symptoms, so discuss it with your doctor.

C_POLLEN.patient_text: Pollen results show sensitization. They matter most if nose, eye or chest symptoms follow the local pollen season. Pollen results can overlap with each other.

C_MOULD.patient_text: Mould results show sensitization. Several moulds can share proteins, so one positive result may reflect another mould. Symptoms in damp seasons or damp rooms are useful clues.

C_YEAST.patient_text: Candida lives on normal skin and in the gut, so a positive result often does not mean an infection or a current problem. Your doctor will read it with your symptoms.

C_DRUG.patient_text: Blood IgE tests are not validated for most medicines, and a negative result never means a medicine is safe. Never start, stop or retry a medicine because of this report.

C_DRUG_ROUTE.patient_text: Many medicine reactions do not involve IgE, and some appear days later. A drug allergy specialist decides what testing or supervised steps are right for you.

C_FOOD.patient_text: A positive food result does not mean you must avoid that food. Do not remove foods you eat without symptoms because of this test alone. Your doctor decides with your history.

C_FOOD_LOWER_PERF.patient_text: Blood tests for this food type are less reliable and are often positive in people who eat these foods without trouble. Your history matters far more than this result.

C_PARASITE.patient_text: IgE to worm proteins may reflect past or present exposure and cannot tell which. Never take worm medicines because of this report, and let your doctor decide on further tests.

C_ANISAKIS.patient_text: Anisakis can cause both infection and allergy after eating infected fish. Tell your doctor about hives, swelling or stomach pain after fish meals, especially raw or lightly cooked fish.
